decision: Rows due within 72 hours turn amber, and the due column counts down live
why: Network deadlines are the only hard constraint in disputes; a missed deadline is an automatic loss regardless of evidence.
alternative: Sort by amount and show the due date as plain text.
value: No dispute is lost to the calendar.

decision: The AI assembles an evidence pack of checkable proofs, each with its source and weight
why: Analysts trust evidence they can see and untick; the win likelihood recalculates as proofs change, so the model's reasoning is inspectable.
alternative: A single AI verdict: fight or accept.
value: Win rate up from 51% to 64% in the case this is modeled on, with a person deciding every submission.

decision: A four-step network timeline (claim, evidence, submit, decision) on every case
why: Disputes take a month; the timeline answers 'what happens next and when' for analysts and for support calls.
value: Fewer escalations asking where a dispute stands.

decision: New disputes arrive as dispute.opened events and the evidence pack starts before anyone opens the case
why: Orders, carrier proofs and device history live in other services; gathering them asynchronously on the event means the pack is ready when a person looks.
alternative: Fetch evidence on demand when the analyst opens the case.
value: Analysts review instead of hunting; the queue in this demo is fed by the in-browser world at $0.

decision: Accepting a loss is a first-class action that labels the case for the fraud model
why: Some claims are cheaper to refund than to fight; recording the decision turns it into training data instead of a silent write-off.
value: Every outcome improves the next score.
